scopeReview: PSO-3.D.1–2: language/religion/ethnicity/gender patterns, sense of place and placemaking, centripetal/centrifugal possibilities. Institutions and exclusion provide explicit mechanisms; diversity is not treated as inevitable conflict. Language, religion and ethnicity remain distinct.
varietyReview: Language service map, crosscutting affiliation table, shared institution model and contested-access map. Other applied tasks cover second-language links, place meanings, proxy limits, gender context, survey definitions, national/local representations and sample support. All five skills, varied keys/difficulty.
repetitionReview: Unlike3.1 one-trait description, the language map supports service provision using complementary preferences. Crosscutting identities, integrative/divisive mechanisms and public-space meanings introduce new tasks. No repeated stems or numeric-only copies.
referenceNote: Official scope and UNESCO diversity definition checked. All institutions, communities and data invented; no stereotyped real groups, copied figures, external student resources or independent human review claims.

questions.correctOption: S-language demand is relatively greater in the south, while both languages have users in every district.
questions.independentReview: Computed S complements20/30/80/90 from R80/70/20/10. Every category is present in each district; relative demand differs but absolute demand needs population denominators.

questions.correctOption: Language and religion need not form identical regional patterns; A and B share a language percentage but differ in religion.
questions.independentReview: Compared A/B R80 each, X80/20; A/C X80 each, R80/20. Marginal percentages do not determine joint individual membership; matching one trait cannot force matching all others.

questions.correctOption: Inclusive shared institutions can act as a centripetal force despite cultural differences.
questions.independentReview: Read the two communities’ directed representation links to one council and the explicit inclusive-decision condition. Cohesion is a possible integrative role, not proof of complete agreement or cultural sameness.

questions.correctOption: Exclusion from a valued place can intensify division; the communities’ difference alone does not make that outcome inevitable.
questions.independentReview: Held shared significance constant and introduced unequal access as the specified mechanism. The map establishes a shared boundary-site context, not inevitable conflict or a uniform response from every resident.

questions.correctOption: The shared language can facilitate connections without necessarily eliminating first-language identities.
questions.independentReview: Separated functional second-language use in trade from home-language replacement and religious uniformity. A possible centripetal connection is conditional on interaction, not evidence that all other differences disappear.

questions.correctOption: Placemaking through practices and symbols connected to a sense of place.
questions.independentReview: Identified deliberate resident practices and symbolic/material space as the placemaking mechanism. No population process or universal sense of belonging is inferred from the festival alone.

questions.correctOption: Funding, history and use can differ, so a building’s dimensions are not a count of affiliated residents.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished material prominence from affiliation counts; no fixed capacity/adherence ratio is provided. The premise itself contradicts universal size-majority inference without asserting anything about a real religion.

questions.correctOption: Social institutions, economic opportunities and cultural expectations may jointly shape the pattern.
questions.independentReview: Matched the proposed multicausal explanation to childcare, employment and expectations. Avoided biological determinism and ecological inference; the question asks what to test rather than claiming a proven causal effect.

questions.correctOption: Collect appropriately defined language-use and self-identified ethnic information separately.
questions.independentReview: Checked the distinction between a language measure and ethnic self-identification. No ranking of ethnic groups, biological criterion or single fixed identity is imposed.

questions.correctOption: A national representation can simplify or omit the diversity visible at local scales.
questions.independentReview: Compared selective national branding with locally differentiated evidence. The inference concerns representation across scales, not a claim that either national belonging or local diversity must be false.

questions.correctOption: Seventy-five percent of surveyed residents support it, but support is not unanimous and the sample alone does not reveal every subgroup’s view.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed300/400=.75 and100/400=.25. Missing subgroup denominators prevent equal-rate inference; population generalization also depends on sampling rather than the total count alone.
